subject: overlaying (adapted) normal density curves on a facetted plot

messages.author: b3ca0c52e87f982f
messages.subject: overlaying (adapted) normal density curves on a facetted plot
parts:
Hello, 

I have a series of histograms/density plots to do, which I would like to present on the same page using facet_wrap (easy). I also would like to display a normal density curve in each panel (easy). But I don't manage how to adapt the mean and sd of the normal density curve in order to match the mean and sd of the data (individually) in each facet. 

Basic example: 
variable <- rep(1:5, each=1000) #my real data is also composed of 5 variables with 1000 values each
x <- rnorm(variable, variable)
dat <- data.frame(variable, x)
ggplot(data=dat, aes(x)) + 
  geom_histogram(aes(y=..density..), col='grey50', fill="grey") + 
  geom_density() + 
  facet_wrap(~variable, scales='free')

I thus would liket to add a normal density curve with mean and sd corresponding to the mean and sd of x in each panel. I suppose stat_function will do the trick. But how to let stat_function compute the actual mean and sd, separately for each panel? 

Thanks a lot for your help. 

Matthieu

messages.subject: Re: overlaying (adapted) normal density curves on a facetted plot
parts: The easiest way is to compute the densities yourself:

xgrid <- seq(min(dat$x), max(dat$x), length = 100)

density <- ddply(dat, "variable", function(df) {
dens <- with(df, dnorm(xgrid, mean(x), sd(x)))
data.frame(x = xgrid, dens)
})

geom_line(aes(y = dens), data = density) +
facet_wrap(~variable, scales='free')

Hadley
